messages:
Aisha (CEO): Thanks for coming to today's all-hands. Leaving a live thread for follow-ups on strategy stuff that came up. Post quick Qs and I'll answer here.
Priya (sales): Quick: customers ask "why Redwood vs a cloud provider offering model endpoints". Short pitch suggested?
Aisha (CEO): Short pitch: "We deliver predictable inference — consistent latency, transparent unit economics, and deployment choices (hosted/dedicated/private) so your SLAs and compliance needs are met." That's the 1-liner.
Ken (eng): For product collateral, can we give one concrete perf number for demos?
Tom (VP Product): Use this: `99th %ile gen latency < 200ms for 1k token median workloads on Dedicated-XL`. Also show cost delta: typical batching + caching gives ~3x token cost reduction vs naive endpoints. Use real benchmark page link when public.
Jules (research): On the roadmap: do we double down on quantized inference support or add more greenfield features like reranking pipelines?
Aisha (CEO): Prioritize quant/serving stability for production customers. Reranking/feature work is important, but the business impact is higher to ship predictable, lower-cost inference first.
Priya (sales): Competitor messaging: is it OK to say we offer "single-tenant SLAs"? Any legal caution?
Tom (VP Product): Factual claims only. Say "single-tenant deployment options with SLA-backed latency targets for Dedicated customers". Don't claim competitor shortcomings. We'll provide approved lines in the battlecard.
Zoe (people-ops): Hiring follow-up: will we be ramping infra hires?
Aisha (CEO): Yes. Next quarter hiring focus: 2 infra engs (serving/runtime), 1 onboarding solutions SE, and 1 product manager for Optimize. We'll share reqs soon.
Ken (eng): Any prioritization guidance between Dedicated autoscaling improvements vs observability for Private installs?
Aisha (CEO): If Private customers are blocked on observability/integrations, prioritize those. Otherwise, Dedicated autoscale and cost controls come first. Customer-led prioritization.
Priya (sales): Can you give me one canned rebuttal for customers saying "we can just host open models ourselves"?
Aisha (CEO): Canned rebuttal: "Self-hosting hides engineering debt: predictable latency, KV caching, runtime optimizations, and ongoing maintenance are what you really buy from us. We turn inference into a product, not a project." Keep it short + empathetic.
Tom (VP Product): I'll upload an internal one-pager and the SLO examples to #product in 30m.
ops-bot: Meeting recording and slides uploaded: https://internal.redwood.example/all-hands/1757664321 (auto) :white_check_mark:
Jules (research): One more: for model catalog strategy, can we clarify criteria for "production-ready"?
Aisha (CEO): Criteria: latency/throughput fit for typical customer workloads, quantization support, reliable tokenization behavior, and basic eval pass (no regressions on core prompts). We'll publish checklist in docs.
Priya (sales): Awesome, thanks. I'll wait for the battlecard.
Aisha (CEO): Thanks all. If you want to discuss objections or roleplay lines, ping me or Tom 1:1. Closing thread. — Aisha
